acts.title: To: recruitment@zhetysu-group.kz
parts: 1 · which job, and where you saw it
text: Subject: Application — Team Leader, Karaganda branch
I am writing to apply for the position of team leader at your Karaganda branch, advertised on the Jobs & Training website this month.

I currently work as an assistant manager in a retail company, where I supervise a team of nine and am responsible for the weekly schedule and for staff training. I have been in the role for three years and was promoted to it from the shop floor.

For example, when two colleagues were made redundant last spring, I reorganized the shift pattern so that the branch stayed open the same hours with a smaller team. Customer satisfaction did not fall, and staff turnover in my department is now the lowest in the region.

I am applying to your company in particular because of its reputation for training its own managers rather than recruiting from outside. I would like to make further progress in management, and I believe I would be well suited to a branch of this size.
Please find attached my CV, which is up to date as of this month. I would be happy to attend an interview at any time, including at short notice.
I look forward to hearing from you.

gives one concrete example with a result
says why this company and not another

is used because the reader’s name is known

acts.title: Said in the room or written on the page?
text: In an interview you can hesitate, check, and ask for the question again. Nobody minds; it shows you are listening.
A letter has one chance. It names the job, gives evidence with a result, and never asks the reader to guess.

write.q: Write an application letter of about 230 words for a job you would genuinely like. Follow the model: which job and where you saw it → what you do now → one concrete example with a result → why this company → CV and interview → the right sign-off.
write.model:
Subject: Application — Sales Team Leader, Karaganda

Dear Ms Karimova,

I am writing to apply for the position of sales team leader advertised on your website this month.

I currently work as a senior sales specialist at an online language school, where I supervise a team of four and am responsible for our reporting and for training new starters. I have been in the role for three years.

For example, last autumn our response time to new enquiries had risen to more than four hours. I rebuilt the way enquiries were assigned and introduced a simple morning check. Within six weeks the average was under thirty minutes, and the conversion rate rose by a fifth.

I am applying to your company in particular because of its reputation for promoting from inside rather than recruiting from outside, and because the Karaganda branch is the one I know best as a customer.

Please find attached my CV, which is up to date as of this month. I would be happy to attend an interview at any time, including at short notice.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Tilek Nurlanov

speak.q: Now do the interview half out loud. Somebody asks you a vague question — “Tell me about a difficult situation.” Ask for clarification first, check you have understood, then answer with one example and a result.
speak.model: Sorry, could you explain what you mean by difficult — difficult with people, or difficult technically? … Right. So, if I understand you correctly, you want a situation where I disagreed with somebody. To give you a good example: last autumn I disagreed with my manager about response times. He thought four hours was normal. I rebuilt the way enquiries were assigned, and within six weeks we were under thirty minutes.
